  <div class="cv-profile">
    <strong>Senior Research Fellow</strong> — Duke-NUS Medical School, Singapore<br>
    Computational behaviour scientist. I build measurement tools for internal states: automated tracking, effect-size estimation, and high-dimensional behavioral benchmarking. I also work with electrophysiology time-series — spike sorting, LFP analysis, and signal conditioning. Currently: epitranscriptomics of native RNA states, ethomics of hunger circuits, constructing LLM loops to produce scientific reasoning and writing. In my spare time I do art and music, and <a href="https://xusangyu.com/blog/08_apple_watch.html">plot my own data for fun on Observable<a>.<br>

  <!-- EXPERIENCE -->
  <h2 class="cv-section-title">Experience</h2>
  <div class="cv-entry">
    <span class="cv-entry-main">Senior Research Fellow &mdash; Duke-NUS Medical School Singapore</span>
    <span class="cv-entry-date">2026–present</span>
  </div>
  <p style="font-size: 0.95rem; color: var(--warm-grey); margin: -0.5rem 0 1.2rem; padding-left: 0.1rem;">
    Computational ethomics pipelines for internal state inference and epitranscriptomics workflows for native RNA modification mapping. Developing agentic LLM evaluation systems for scientific reasoning — grounded analytical outputs feed adversarial multi-agent critique and structured manuscript assessment pipelines.
  </p>
  <div class="cv-entry">
    <span class="cv-entry-main">Senior Research Fellow / Research Fellow &mdash; IMCB, A*STAR Singapore</span>
    <span class="cv-entry-date">2017–2026</span>
  </div>
  <p style="font-size: 0.95rem; color: var(--warm-grey); margin: -0.5rem 0 1.2rem; padding-left: 0.1rem;">
    Wrote and won a SGD 300,000 National Medical Research Council Young Individual Research Grant as sole investigator; ran it for four years (2021–2025) with one research assistant, whom I trained in genetics, assay development, automatic behavior tracking and pose estimation, machine learning, and native RNA sequencing.<br>
    Co-developed DABEST 2.0, an estimation statistics framework for visualising effect sizes and uncertainty; predecessor has 2,000+ citations. Built DESTRA, a ground-truth-referenced benchmarking approach for high-dimensional behavioural states, showing that perturbations can shift individual metrics without recapitulating the full target state — presented as an invited talk at APDNC3 / RIKEN 2024.<br>
    Developed automated behavioural classification pipelines for large-scale ethological data; contributed to novel optogenetic silencing tools (<em>Nature Communications</em> 2024) and long-Stokes-shift fluorescent markers for two-photon imaging (<em>microPublication Biology</em> 2026).
  </p>

  <div class="cv-entry">
    <span class="cv-entry-main">Postdoctoral Associate &mdash; Tonegawa Lab, MIT</span>
    <span class="cv-entry-date">2016–2017</span>
  </div>
  <p style="font-size: 0.95rem; color: var(--warm-grey); margin: -0.5rem 0 1.2rem; padding-left: 0.1rem;">
    Designed the first olfactory-cued rodent intertemporal choice task, translating a paradigm from human preference evaluation to allow precise neural recording at the decision point. Built a psychometric model predicting choice probability as a function of delay; dorsal raphe serotonergic activation increased patience while silencing drove impulsivity. <em>in vivo</em> optrode electrophysiology of dorsal raphe neurons. (<em>Current Biology</em> 2017, co-corresponding). Also contributed to studies of noradrenergic attentional circuits (<em>PNAS</em> 2020) and basolateral amygdala valence encoding (<em>Nature Neuroscience</em> 2016).
  </p>
